output: {"answers":{"d05":"阳性不一定意味着患病，因为还差一个关键数字：基础患病率。假设10000人里患病率1%，即100个病人；检测灵敏度99%，能查出其中99人。但9900个健康人里假阳性率5%，会误报495人。于是594个阳性中，真正的病人只占99÷594≈17%。这就是贝叶斯公式：P(患病|阳性)=P(阳性|患病)×P(患病)÷P(阳性)。它把「病人测出阳性的概率」换成「阳性者是病人的概率」——方向正好相反，必须用患病率给两边加权：分母是所有会测出阳性的人（真病人加被误报的健康人）。改变一个条件看结果：同样的检测换到患病率10%的高危人群，阳性后患病的概率跳到约69%。检测准确率没变，先验一变，结论就大不一样。","d03":"正反馈放大变化，是因为「结果」顺着同一方向加强了「原因」，让小差异绕着回路滚雪球。典型过程：麦克风靠近音箱，拾进一点杂音，音箱放大后播出，麦克风再拾进更大的声音，再放大……几秒内就啸叫刺耳。每绕一圈加一层，变化按倍数而非加法增长。气候里同样如此：冰雪反射阳光使地面更冷，更冷又造出更多冰雪。要说清的是：「正」指方向——变化被同向加强，不是指「好」。银行挤兑、谣言扩散也是正反馈，后果却是崩坏；回路放大什么取决于起点，它本身不辨好坏。放大也不能无限持续：啸叫被音量上限卡住，冰盖受海洋面积限制，达到饱和就停。与之相对，负反馈把偏移拉回来，比如空调恒温。判断一个系统是稳还是险，先找有没有「越X就越更X」的同向回路。","v08":"Little's law says: average number of customers in a system (L) = arrival rate (λ) × average time each spends there (W). Why multiply? Picture a coffee shop steady at 10 customers inside. If each stays 5 minutes, the shop must admit 10 ÷ 5 = 2 per minute; rearranged, L = 2 × 5 = 10. Total customer-minutes inside equals arrivals per minute times minutes each — much like distance = speed × time. It also works backwards: orders arrive at 100/hour and each spends 0.25 hours being processed, so about 25 orders are in flight. Cut waiting time W and, with λ unchanged, work-in-progress L falls proportionally. The law holds only in steady state — inflow equals outflow, no draining or exploding queue — yet it assumes nothing about arrival patterns or service order, which is why it fits coffee shops, CPUs, and ticket queues alike.","v03":"自然选择改变种群的方式是筛选，不是努力：个体不能把自己练成更适应的样子；能遗传的差异先随机出现，环境只决定哪些差异留下更多后代。以长颈鹿为例。经典误解是「为了够到高处的叶子，脖子越伸越长」。实际过程是：群体里脖子本来就有长有短，且差异可以遗传。低处叶子被吃光时，长脖个体吃得更多、活得更好、留下的后代更多——注意「吃得多」并不改变它自己的脖子，改变的是下一代群体里长脖基因的比例。许多代之后种群整体脖子变长，是长脖个体占比升高，不是每只鹿都被拉长了。两个关键点：变异发生在繁殖之前，不问方向；环境不「制造」适应性，只做淘汰。若条件反过来，比如食物只在高处变成只在低处，原有优势消失，趋势就会停止甚至反转。","v06":"Deadlock is when processes each hold a resource and wait for the other's — so none can ever proceed. Small example: Transaction A locks row 1; Transaction B locks row 2. A then asks for row 2 while B asks for row 1. Each waits for the other to release, and neither ever will, because they only release after finishing. They wait forever. Four conditions must all hold: mutual exclusion (one holder per resource), hold-and-wait, no preemption (you can't take a lock away), and circular wait. Break any one and deadlock becomes impossible — which is where the fixes come from: acquire locks in a fixed global order (kills circular wait), request everything upfront (kills hold-and-wait), or time out and abort one victim. Notice the contrast with an ordinary wait: here waiting is mutual, so time doesn't help. A third transaction holding nothing can still run — deadlock starves its victims, not necessarily the whole system.","v05":"信息熵衡量「结果揭晓之前你有多不确定」：概率摊得越平，熵越大。公式 H = −Σ pᵢ log₂ pᵢ，输入每个选项的概率，算出平均需要多少个是/否问题（比特）才能确定结果。为什么均匀分布最不确定？因为完全平的概率对每个选项一视同仁，你没有任何理由押某一个；一旦概率倾斜，就有了「更可能」的选项，猜它常常猜中，不确定性随之下降。极端情形：某项概率为1，结果毫无悬念，熵为0。均匀硬币的熵是1比特；灌铅后正面概率0.9，熵只有约0.47——多数时候结果早已注定。对数的作用是让不确定性可相加：连掷两次均匀硬币，熵正好翻倍。改变条件：选项数固定时均匀最大；选项增多（公平骰子的熵约2.58比特），熵也升高——可分辨的可能性越多，揭晓前越难押中。","v01":"过拟合是模型把学习材料「背下来」而不是「学规律」，结果练习题满分，遇到新题就错。比如教程序识别垃圾邮件：若它记住「凡出现『恭喜您』三个字就是垃圾邮件」，换一批邮件就失效。更极端的是让模型死记所有历史考题的答案，练习时百分百正确，可它记住的是每道题本身而非解题规律，新题一道都答不对。判断办法很直接：拿没参与训练的新数据测一下。训练成绩高、新数据明显掉，就是过拟合。常见成因是模型太灵活、数据太少——参数多到能替每个旧样本「定制答案」。所以对策要么增加数据，要么限制模型复杂度，逼它只能学共同规律。一头对照：模型太简单会「欠拟合」，连训练数据都学不好，规律和新数据都差。过拟合恰在另一头：训练漂亮，泛化糟糕。","d01":"似然和后验概率用同一个公式算数，但回答的问题方向相反。概率问「假设定下后，数据会是什么样」；似然问「数据已经看到，某个假设的可能性有多大」。例子：桌上的硬币要么正常（假设A），要么两面都是正面（假设B）。掷三次全正面。P(三正|A)=1/8，P(三正|B)=1。这两个数是概率，也是似然：固定这批数据，B的似然更大——数据更「配得上」B。后验概率回答的是下一步的问题：「看完数据，我该信B到什么程度」，记作P(B|三正)。贝叶斯公式用似然乘上先验，再归一化得到后验。注意似然大不等于后验大：若你有十足把握桌上只有正常硬币，先验直接排除B，三次正面也翻不了案。所以有限数据永远只是「更支持」，不是证实；继续掷下去，全正面的连击才让A越来越难维持。","d07":"相关只说明两个数字一起涨落，因果还要求「谁推动谁」。把相关当成因果，会开出无效的药方。例子：某城市统计发现，冰淇淋销量越高，溺水人数越多，两者高度相关。若据此禁售冰淇淋，溺水不会减少——因为真正的推手是第三个因素：天气热。天热让人既买冰淇淋又下河游泳，两者是同一原因的两个结果，这叫「混杂变量」；冰淇淋和溺水之间没有直接通道。另一种假因果来自方向颠倒：「消防员人数与火灾损失正相关」，不是消防员造成损失，而是大火招来更多消防员。判断因果需要能「改变一个，看另一个是否跟着变」：控制天气做对照，冰淇淋销量不同而溺水相同，因果链就断了。所以看到相关先问三件事：有没有共同原因？方向会不会反？是不是巧合？能设计干预实验时，答案才最硬。","d02":"Variance measures how spread out numbers are around their average. Two classes can both average 70, yet one sits between 65 and 75 while the other ranges from 20 to 100 — variance captures that difference. To compute it: take each value's distance from the mean, square each distance, then average the squares — variance = mean of (x − μ)². With values 4 and 6: mean 5, deviations −1 and +1, variance = (1+1)/2 = 1. Why square? Deviations above and below the mean cancel to zero if you just add them, so squaring makes every distance count. Squaring also punishes big outliers harder: one value 10 away contributes 100, while ten values each 1 away contribute 10 total — an emphasis on large deviations, a design choice rather than the only option. Since squaring changes units (points become points²), taking the square root gives the standard deviation, back in original units.","d08":"Compound growth means growth applies to the accumulated total, not just the original amount, so gains themselves start earning gains. At 10% a year, 100 becomes 110 in year 1, but year 2 adds 11 — interest charged on 110, not 100. The formula is 100 × 1.10ⁿ: the exponent turns steady percentages into acceleration. 1.10¹⁰ ≈ 2.59, so ten years gives 259, not 200; at 20%, 1.20¹⁰ ≈ 6.19. Why the starting amount matters: with the same rate and time, results scale proportionally. Growing at 10% for ten years, 1,000 becomes 2,590 and 10,000 becomes 25,900 — identical percentage growth, very different absolute gains, because compound growth multiplies whatever base you give it; a bigger base is simply more principal for the exponent to act on. The same logic explains why early contributions win: money deposited sooner compounds through more years, so 1,000 saved now outranks 1,000 saved a decade later.","d06":"A cache stores a copy of data close by so your app doesn't rebuild it on every request. Cache invalidation is deciding when that copy is stale and must be deleted or refreshed. Example: a web store caches each product page — built once, then served from memory to every visitor. When the merchant changes the price, the cached page still shows the old one. Invalidation means deleting that cached page the instant the price updates, so the next request rebuilds it from the database. The hard part is timing: invalidate too rarely and users see wrong prices; too often and the cache stops saving work. Two common policies: expire after 60 seconds (time-based), or delete the key whenever the underlying data changes (event-based). Coverage is the tricky part — one price change also affects the product list, search results, and recommendations; miss one affected key and a stale page survives. That's why invalidation is famously called a hard problem.","v04":"Idempotency means doing the same operation twice has the same effect as doing it once. It matters in distributed systems because networks are unreliable: when your payment request times out, you can't tell whether it failed or only the response was lost — so clients must retry. If \"charge $100\" isn't idempotent, a retry double-charges the customer. The standard fix: attach a unique request ID to each operation. The server records processed IDs; a repeat carrying a seen ID returns the stored result instead of executing again. Compare: \"add 100 to balance\" duplicates under retry, while \"create charge with idempotency key K\" doesn't. Idempotent doesn't mean read-only — deleting an already-deleted item returns \"not found,\" but the end state matches a single delete, so it still counts. Design rule: anything a retry can reach must be idempotent, either naturally or via keys.","v02":"Precision and recall measure two different ways a search can fail. Suppose you search a library catalog for books on ocean pollution, and the system returns 10 results: 6 are actually relevant, while 400 relevant books sit uncited in the stacks. Precision asks: of what it returned, how much was right? 6/10 = 60% — it measures noise, wrong items pushed at you. Recall asks: of everything relevant, how much did it find? 6/406 ≈ 1.5% — it measures silence, good items missed. The two can trade off: return only the single most certain hit and precision nears 100% while recall collapses; dump every book into the results and recall hits 100% while precision craters. Which to prioritize depends on which mistake costs more: spam filters prize precision (flagging real mail is costly), cancer screening prizes recall (missing a case is costly). Both fractions share true positives on top; the denominators differ — returned versus relevant.","d04":"Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you gave up — not all options, just the top one you would have picked instead. With a free afternoon you could study for an exam, earn $60 at a shift, or nap. If you choose the shift, your opportunity cost is the exam prep, since that's your next-best use of the time — not \"studying plus napping plus everything else.\" This reframes \"free\" activities: a free movie still costs whatever else those two hours could have done. No money leaves your pocket, but time is spent either way. Two refinements: compare against the single best alternative only — adding up every forgone option double-counts; and ignore sunk costs — if you already bought a non-refundable ticket, that money is gone regardless, so the real choice is \"attend vs. next-best thing,\" not \"get my money's worth.\" The habit to build: before committing, ask, \"compared with what?\"","v07":"公共物品是「每个人都能用，且一个人的使用不减少别人份额」的东西：路灯、国防、防洪堤、干净空气。两个特征缺一不可：无法轻易排除别人使用（非排他），多人同时用也不互相挤占（非竞争）。面包是反例——不付钱就吃不到，一人吃掉别人就没得吃，所以市场能高效供应面包；路灯却没法只给付过钱的人照亮。问题由此产生：不管谁出钱，路人都能受益。既然不出钱也照用不误，个体就倾向少出钱、等别人埋单，这就是搭便车。结果是人人都在等，路灯根本建不起来——明明人人受益，却没人愿意付钱。这正是市场失灵：对大家有价值的物品，靠自愿交易供应不出来。常见解法是用税收强制分摊（政府修路、养军队），或人为造出排他性（加密收费频道、专利授权）。条件变化：一旦某项物品能收费（公园设闸门卖票），性质就滑向「俱乐部物品」，私人投资便愿意进入了。"}
